title: Ripuarian Franks
capsule: The Ripuarian Franks ('river Franks') were a confederation of Frankish tribes settled along the Rhine and Moselle rivers, with their chief center at Colonia Agrippinensium (Cologne), distinguished in early medieval sources from the Salian Franks to the northwest. They appear in Roman sources from the 3rd century as raiders and subsequently as foederati, and their law code, the Lex Ribuaria, was compiled in the 7th century under Merovingian auspices. Clovis I incorporated the Ripuarian territories by defeating their king Sigebert the Lame and his son Chloderic around 509–510 CE, absorbing them into the unified Frankish kingdom, after which the Ripuarians ceased to exist as a separate political entity though Ripuarian customary law persisted for generations.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Ripuarian Franks are attested in Roman and Merovingian narrative sources, but they were never a unified polity with fixed borders; any territorial polygon is a schematic reconstruction.
